text:
Traffic Tech inc. c. Maiore

2021 QCCS 2246

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

No.:

500-17-116953-210

DATE:

June 3
rd
2021

_____________________________________________________________________

BY

THE HONOURABLE

SYLVAIN LUSSIER, J.S.C.

_____________________________________________________________________

TRAFFIC TECH INC.

Plaintiffs

v.

FRANK
MAIORE

ASHLEY
PAQUET

KATHERINE
ZBOCH

and

673753 ONTARIO LIMITÉE

Defendants

JUDGMENT

(On
Motion for the Issuance of a Provisional Injunction)

_____________________________________________________________________

THE CONTEXT

[
1
]

Plaintiff seeks to obtain an order for
provisional, interlocutory and permanent injunction and, subsequently, an order
for damages as a result of alleged violations of legal and contractual
post-employment obligations, namely duty of loyalty, failure to give reasonable
notice of termination,  non-competition, non-solicitation and confidentiality
to which the Defendants Frank Maiore
[1]
, Ashley
Paquet,
[2]
and Katherine Zboch
[3]
were subject to and for which 673753 Ontario Limitée, operating
under the name  “Traffix” would be complicit in the breach of these
obligations;

[
2
]

Plaintiff, Traffic Tech Inc.
[4]
specializes
in arranging for the transportation of goods, warehousing and other related
services in the territory of North America. Traffic Tech is a non-asset based,
third-party logistics company responsible for arranging the transportation and
warehousing of goods on behalf of their customers throughout the world.

[
3
]

It has operated in the transportation brokerage
industry for over thirty years.  The company has expanded to over a thousand
employees worldwide, the majority of which are located in the province of
Quebec;

[
4
]

Maiore, Paquet and Zboch were employed by
Traffic Tech, until they resigned on May 18
th
, 2021 and commenced
employment for Traffix on May 19
th
2021.

[
5
]

Traffix is a company that specializes in
arranging for the transportation of goods, warehousing and other related
services in the territory of North America, and is consequently a competitor to
Traffic Tech.

[
6
]

Maiore was hired by Traffic Tech as an executive
account manager on September 6
th
2006, position he held until his
resignation. At the time of his hiring, he earned $8,333.33 a month. When he
left, he was earning $6,250 monthly, plus a bonus of 30% of gross profit, a
change in remuneration which was unilaterally imposed in October 2020.

[
7
]

In early 2021, Traffic Tech imposed a $10
tracking fee per load, reducing the gross profit on each load, and thereby
reducing his commission.

[
8
]

He entered into an employment contract
[5]
which provides for a confidentiality
covenant, but does not contain a non-competition or a non-solicitation obligation.
The contract also provided for him to give a notice of termination or
resignation of “at least four weeks”
[6]
.

[
9
]

Paquet was employed by Traffic Tech, as a
customer service representative, on two  separate occasions, the first period from
October 1
st
, 2003 to January 31
st
, 2014 and the second
period from September 19
th
, 2014 to May 18
th
, 2021;

[
10
]

Paquet entered into an employment contract
[7]
which provided for the
signature of a  “Non-Competition and Non Solicitation Agreement”

[8]
reading as follows:

1.02 The Employee agrees that
in the event that the Employee resigns their employment with the Company that
he/she will not anywhere in the Greater Montreal Area, directly or indirectly,
carry on, act as an agent for, be employed by or become otherwise associated
with another firm, business or corporation which would be in competition with
the activities of the Employer at the date of cessation of the employment
including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, contacting,
soliciting or carrying on business with any customer, customer or sales lead
known to be entered in the database of the Company or that became known to the
Employee through his/her employment with the Company, for a period of six (6)
months following the date of resignation from said employment;

[
11
]

Furthermore, this Agreement provided for the
non-solicitation of customers and employees of Traffic Tech, for a period of
one year following her resignation. The non-solicitation covenant read as
follows:

2.01 The Employee agrees that during the term of his/her employment
with the Company and for a period of one (1) year following the date of
termination of such employment for any reason whatsoever, he/she shall not,
either directly, or indirectly, for his/her own benefit or for the benefit of
any person, enterprise or entity, solicit or attempt to solicit the business of
any customer of the Company who may have made a purchase from or requested a
quote for services from the Company in the period of one (1) year preceding the
date of termination of the Employee’s employment;

2.02 The Employee agrees that during the term of his/her employment
with the Company and for a period of one (1) year following the date of
termination of such employment for any reason whatsoever, he/she shall not,
either directly or indirectly, for his/her own benefit or for the benefit of
any person, enterprise or entity, entice, encourage or hire any employee of the
Company to end their employment relationship with the Company or to breach any
contract with or obligation owed to the Company, without obtaining the prior
written consent of the Company.

[
12
]

Zboch was hired by Traffic Tech as a customer
service representative on December 17
th
, 2018, a position she held
until her resignation on May 18
th
, 2021. Her employment contract
[9]
contained provisions similar
to Paquet’s contract.

[
13
]

Neither contract provided for a notice period in
case of resignation.

[
14
]

On May 18, 2021 at 17h00, Maiore, Paquet and
Zboch simultaneously provided their resignation letters to Traffic Tech’s human
resources’ department via e-mail
[10]

and copied their respective managers. Their resignation was effective
immediately.

[
15
]

Maiore returned his corporate cellular device
and the building key card to Ms. Heidi Ross, project manager of Traffic Tech, minutes
following his resignation.
Paquet and Zboch’s
corporate cellular devices and other property belonging to Traffic Tech, including
files entitled “carrier rates and customer rates”, as well as sensitive documents
belonging to Traffic Tech were returned by a Traffix courier on May 19
th
,
2021.

[
16
]

Traffic Tech asserts that Maiore, Paquet and
Zboch purposely deleted information which was saved on their corporate cellular
devices, whether it be text messages, contacts, or anything else of importance.

[
17
]

Maiore, Paquet and Zboch deny any tempering
with the cellular phones, except for Maiore who admits having deleted a “handful
of personal phone numbers and information belonging to my family members”
[11]
.

[
18
]

All three defendants call the Court’s attention
to Traffic Tech’s “Acceptable Use of the Internet Policy”
[12]
which warns employees that “deleting or erasing information,
documents or messages on Traffic Tech’s electronic devices is, in most cases, ineffective”.

[
19
]

On May 19
th
2021, Maiore, Paquet and
Zboch simultaneously updated their LinkedIn profiles to announce their
employment with Traffix
[13]
.

[
20
]

Traffic Tech asserts that on May 19
th
, Maiore solicited the services of Traffic
Tech’s long-standing customer, The Children’s Place.

[
21
]

It is also alleged that Maiore
attempted  to obtain a quote from Goa Logistics, Traffic Tech’s supplier, in
order to service The Children’s Place, Traffic Tech’s customer.

[
22
]

On May 20
th
2021, Traffic Tech sent
individualized cease and desist letters
[14]

to each of the Defendants, asking that that they “immediately cease working at
Traffix” and that they supply requested information outlined in the letter.

[
23
]

On May 21
st
2021, attorneys for
Traffix answered on behalf of their clients denying that they had engaged in
any illegal conduct or that they had given any confidential information to
Traffix
[15]
.

[
24
]

Traffic Tech complains
that “they failed to address any of the points that
Traffic Tech addressed in their letter and failed to address the clear
instances of breaches that the Defendants conducted”.

[
25
]

Consequently, Traffic Tech asserts that
defendants breached  their duty of loyalty and contractual obligations and
seeks from this Court  an order prohibiting Frank Maiore, Ashley Paquet
and Katherine Zboch from offering their services to 673753 Ontario Limitée and
to compete with Traffic Tech Inc. for a period of ten days following the
issuance of the provisional injunction order, and prohibiting, for the same
period, 673753 Ontario Limitée from hiring or otherwise retaining the services
of Frank Maiore, Ashley Paquet and Katherine Zboch.

[
26
]

The proceeding further seeks non-solicitation
orders, and demands that confidential information and other property be
returned to Traffic Tech.

QUESTION AT ISSUE

[
27
]

Should the Court grant the requested restraining order and
accessory measures?

[
28
]

For the reasons that follow, no order will be
issued at this stage of the proceedings.

DISCUSSION

A.

Criteria Applicable to the Issuance of an Interlocutory Injunction

[
29
]

In the recent case of
Groupe CRH Canada inc
. c.
Beauregard
,
[16]
the Court of Appeal
reformulated the three pronged test for the issuance of an interlocutory
injunction, updating the concepts the Court has to analyze.

[
30
]

The Court establishes :

[28
]         Premièrement,
une étude préliminaire du fond du litige doit établir qu'il y a une question
sérieuse à juger. Ce critère est généralement peu exigeant. Il suffit que la
demande ne soit ni frivole ni vexatoire. Par conséquent, un long examen du
bien-fondé de la demande n'est souvent ni nécessaire ni souhaitable sauf circonstances
exceptionnelles – comme lorsque l’injonction interlocutoire équivaut
pratiquement à une disposition définitive du litige.

[…]

[30]      Deuxièmement, il faut rechercher si
la partie qui requiert l’injonction interlocutoire subirait un préjudice irréparable
si sa demande était rejetée. Le C.p.c. ajoute ici la notion de « préjudice
sérieux ». Un préjudice irréparable est un préjudice qui n’est pas
susceptible d’être remédié par des dommages-intérêts ou qui peut difficilement
l’être.

[…]

[34]         Troisièmement, il faut
rechercher laquelle des deux parties subira le plus grand préjudice selon que
l’injonction interlocutoire sera accordée ou refusée dans l'attente d'une
décision sur le bien-fondé du dossier au mérite. Il s’agit d’un critère jurisprudentiel
qui n’a pas été formellement repris au C.p.c. Les facteurs qui peuvent être
considérés lors de l'examen de ce critère de la « prépondérance des
inconvénients » sont nombreux, et ils varient d'un cas à l'autre.

[
31
]

To these criteria, in the case of a provisional injunction, urgency
has to be established:

Ces éléments
doivent, au surplus, être appréciés dans un contexte où l'urgence doit
prédominer.
[17]

[
32
]

It
is accordingly in order to apply this test to the present instance, with a
particular emphasis on irreparable harm, as dictated by the Court of Appeal.

[
33
]

As Justice Frédéric Bachand, then a member of this
Court, wrote in
La Presse (2018) inc.
c.
Jutras
[18]
:

[6] Il importe de garder à l’esprit que, au
stade provisoire, ces critères doivent être

appliqués avec
« beaucoup plus de rigueur » compte tenu du caractère  « extrêmement
exceptionne[l] et urgen[t] » de l’intervention de la Cour, et que « s’il y
a le moindre doute[,] la demande doit être rejetée »

B.

Urgency

[
34
]

The urgency criteria is easily met. Matters
involving the violation of non-competition agreements are usually urgent.

[
35
]

The Court is satisfied that Traffic Tech has acted
diligently.

C.

Serious Issue to be Tried

[36]

Defendants contest, on different grounds, that
there is not even a serious issue to be tried here. According to them, there is
not even a “colour of right” (
apparence de droit
) in favor of Plaintiff.

[37]

While the first criteria of the test has a low
threshold, defendants may establish that there is no appearance of right, and
consequently, no serious issue to be tried
[19]
.

a)

Frank Maiore

[38]

Maiore did not sign a non-competition agreement,
even if he is the senior employee of the group.

[39]

In the absence of a non-competition undertaking,
post-employment obligations are much less stringent. Marie-France Bich, then a
professor, remarkably summarizes the legal principles applicable to such
employees
[20]
:

... la liberté de
l'ex-salarié ne peut pas être indéfiniment restreinte au nom de la protection
des intérêts de l'employeur (comme le montre d'ailleurs le reste du texte de
Me Vachon): cela aussi fait partie de ce monde de concurrence que doit
affronter l'employeur. Si ce dernier veut protéger ses investissements, qu'il
négocie une clause de non-concurrence (valable). Le second alinéa de
l'article 2088 ne peut pas suppléer aux effets de la négligence de
l'employeur qui a oublié ou omis de négocier ou d'imposer une clause de
non-concurrence ou qui en a mal mesuré la nécessité….

Le deuxième
principe veut que le second alinéa de l'article 2088 soit et doive
être interprété restrictivement puisqu'il fait exception à ce postulat de base
de notre organisation sociale qu'est la liberté de concurrence et de travail…

Troisième
principe, enfin: le contenu obligationnel précis du devoir de loyauté et de
discrétion post-contractuel est affaire d'espèce et dépend d'une variété de
facteurs: nature particulière de l'emploi et de l'entreprise, durée du service
du salarié au sein de l'entreprise, positionnement hiérarchique du salarié dans
l'entreprise et niveau de responsabilités, existence de liens privilégiés du
salarié avec la clientèle de l'employeur, accès à des renseignements
confidentiels, etc…. Il y a des salariés dont la capacité de nuisance
post-contractuelle est à toutes fins utiles inexistante …

Il découle de ces
principes que, de manière générale, le salarié qui quitte l'employeur est libre
de mettre au service d'autrui ou de sa propre entreprise l'expertise, les
connaissances, les qualités qui sont siennes, et cela même s'il les a acquises
ou enrichies au service de l'employeur: … Il peut de même, normalement, faire
immédiatement concurrence à son ex-employeur et cela de diverses façons: en se
mettant au service d'un concurrent, en fondant sa propre entreprise
concurrente, en devenant actionnaire d'une entreprise concurrente, etc., et en
cherchant à s'approprier la clientèle de l'ex-employeur.

Ce faisant,
cependant, le salarié ne doit pas user de moyens malhonnêtes, frauduleux ou
abusifs (comme par exemple le dénigrement, les fausses représentations, les
tromperies, les actes de désorganisation ou de parasitisme); il ne doit pas non
plus se servir de renseignements confidentiels ou de biens (matériels ou
intellectuels) qu'il se serait appropriés pendant son séjour chez
l'ex-employeu; il ne doit pas détourner à son profit ou celui d'un tiers des
occasions d'affaires dont il aurait pris connaissance chez l'ex-employeur.
Bref, le salarié, à la cessation du contrat de travail, ne doit pas faire à son
ancien employeur une concurrence dont les modalités vont à l'encontre des
exigences de la bonne foi.

Quelques
précisions s'imposent en matière de sollicitation de clientèle de même qu'en
matière de protection des renseignements confidentiels.

Sollicitation
de clientèle
.
La clientèle, on le sait, est au coeur de la concurrence et il n'y a donc rien
d'étonnant à ce que l'employeur cherche à la protéger avec énergie et même
acharnement. La clientèle, toutefois, n'appartient à personne, comme le
rappelle volontiers la jurisprudence, et l'ex-salarié peut donc tenter de se
l'approprier ou de la divertir vers son nouvel employeur. Deux réserves à cela.
D'une part, les tribunaux sont assez sévères à l'endroit des ex-salariés qui
font de la sollicitation à l'aide de listes de
clients confidentielles subtilisées à l'employeur avant ou au moment
du départ (n'allant généralement pas, toutefois, jusqu'à leur interdire la
publicité générale). On notera quand même que toute liste de clients (même
subtilisée) n'est pas confidentielle et n'entraînera pas nécessairement la
constatation d'une violation de l'article
2088
. …. D'autre
part, dans les cas où l'ex-salarié avait des rapports privilégiés avec la
clientèle de l'employeur, il pourra lui être interdit de la solliciter pendant
un certain temps après son départ ou plus exactement de la solliciter au moyen
d'approches individuelles et personnalisée. Les moyens de sollicitation
généraux et publics (annonces dans les médias, par exemple) demeurent cependant
permis.

[40]

The
prima

facie
evidence filed by
both parties does not satisfy the Court that Maiore engaged in disloyal
conduct. The fact that he spoke to Traffix weeks before his resignation is hardly
evidence of bad faith, but only of practical reality. He cannot just walk in at
Traffix and request employment.

[41]

The fact that Paquet and Zboch left with him is
explained in their sworn declarations. It is not a concerted effort to leave as
a group, nor a manoeuver to destabilize Traffic Tech.  Paquet and Zboch were
dissatisfied with their employment at Traffic Tech, and did not want to stay if
Maiore, with whom they had a pleasant working relationship, did not stay.

[42]

Maiore did inform his customers that he had left
Traffic Tech. As clearly appears in the article of Me Bich, he had the right to
do so
[21]
.

[43]

The Court does not, on the basis of the limited
evidence, find that there is unwarranted solicitation, being an insistent and
repeated communication in order to divert business
[22]
. The sworn declarations
establish, for the time being, that Children’s Place was dissatisfied with
Traffic Tech’s services and was looking for other suppliers.

[44]

The Court adopts the comments of Justice
Christian Immer in
8782601 Canada inc. (Impact
Échafaudage)
c.
White
:

[23]
Les demanderesses avancent donc qu’il est
« manifeste » que White ait sollicité Robert Hardy inc. et elles en
viennent à cette conclusion par la voie de présomptions. Or, le Tribunal doit
être en mesure d’apprécier, prima facie, les faits qui donnent lieu aux
présomptions que tirent les demanderesses. De tels faits sont absents ou
manifestement insuffisants.

[25
]
Le Tribunal ne voit donc aucune preuve de sollicitation, c’est-à-dire
des démarches pressantes et insistantes, auprès de Robert Hardy inc. ou de tout
autre client. Les demanderesses n’ont donc établi aucune apparence de droit à
cet égard.

[45]

Complaints about resorting to Goa, a carrier,
are equally unwarranted. There is no exclusive right to a common carrier, who
is free to contract with whom it wants.

[46]

The Court is also satisfied that Maiore
immediately remitted to Traffic Tech any proprietary or confidential material,
did not keep a copy or share it with Traffix. It was only handed to a Traffix
employee for the purpose of its return. This comment is equally valid for
Paquet and Zboch.

[47]

Traffic Tech argues that Maiore did not give it
reasonable notice of his resignation. Traffic Tech argues that it should have
received
at least
four weeks, as per the employment agreement. While
article 2091 C.C.Q. requests “reasonable notice”, in this case, the parties have
contractually agreed on the length thereof.

[48]

Whether or not Traffic Tech always fires
resigning employees on the spot will be left to an eventual trial on the
merits.

[49]

It is not serious on the part of Maiore to argue
that he had forgotten the terms of his contract. This being said, while failure
to give reasonable notice on the part of the employee gives rise to an eventual
claim for damages,
[23]
it is not ground for the issuance of an
injunction, whether mandatory or negatory. Authors Bouchard and Sirois
summarize the state of the jurisprudence on the matter:
[24]

La requête en injonction n'est pas le recours utile
pour forcer un salarié démissionnaire à travailler durant le préavis requis
selon l'
article
2091
C.c.Q.
Un auteur mentionne que sous le régime français, la coutume de
Paris appliquée en Nouvelle-France forçait les serviteurs à demeurer chez leurs
maîtres et, en cas de désertion, prohibait à toute personne de les embaucher.
On ne saurait guère se servir de cette base historique malgré que
l'
article
1601 C.c.Q.
permette
l'exécution en nature par voie judiciaire. D'autres auteurs affirment que
l'exécution forcée en nature présente peu d'intérêt pour l'employeur victime
d'une démission illégale de la part du salarié. C'est aussi la solution des
tribunaux judiciaires de common law comme le rapportent les auteurs Barnacle et
Wood. …Ajoutons que le droit de résiliation unilatéral du contrat de travail à
durée indéterminée (quel que soit le motif) ne justifie pas un droit apparent à
la réintégration du salarié démissionnaire. L'injonction n'est pas le bon
recours, car la résiliation est sans motif et possible en tout temps. (References
omitted)

[50]

The Court comes to the conclusion that Traffic
Tech has not appearance of right against Maiore. There is consequently no issue
to be tried.

b)

Paquet and Zboch

[51]

Paquet and Zboch have signed a non-competition
agreement even though they were the subordinates of Maiore, who did not sign
one. According to Article 2089 (3) C.C.Q., the employer has the burden to
establish that such a stipulation is valid. Amongst the items it must establish
is its necessity “for the protection of the legitimate
interests of the employer”
[25]
.

[52]

In light of Maiore’s terms of employment, one
wonders why it is necessary for the protection of Traffic Tech’s interests to
impose non-competition obligations on customer service
representatives, which have no direct contact with customers.

[53]

Their job is to look for trucks and warehouses.

[54]

Paquet and Zboch also raise the fact that the
non-competition clause is overbroad in terms of its scope, since it prohibits
them from being employed by or become otherwise associated with another firm,
business or corporation which would be in competition with the activities of the
Employer, and that, in any capacity whatsoever.

[55]

Justice Bachand, in
La Presse
c.
Jutras
,
quoting Justice Jean-Pierre Sénécal, wrote :

[18] Ces dispositions vont encore plus loin que celles
que le juge Jean-Pierre

Sénécal a considérées invalides dans
Ikon Solutions
de bureau inc.
c
. Docu-Plus

Conseillers en gestion de documents inc.
[26]
. Il y écrivait notamment ce qui suit :

Les clauses visent beaucoup trop large, comme
on l’a déjà dit. Outre ce qui a été mentionné précédemment […], elles empêchent
même un employé d’occuper dans une entreprise concurrente de [l’ancien
employeur] à peu près toute fonction, même si celle-ci n’a rien à voir avec les
activités antérieurement exercées pour [cet ancien employeur]. La clause telle
que rédigée empêche en fait tout défendeur antérieurement employé par [l’ancien
employeur] de travailler pour [le nouvel employeur], même comme balayeur,
concierge ou cuisinier au siège social [de ce nouvel employeur].

[56]

These considerations cast serious doubts on the
validity and applicability of Paquet and Zboch’s non-compete covenants. It
cannot be said, at this stage of the file, that here is no appearance of right.
While weak, there may remain an issue to be tried. It is safer to examine the
irreparable harm criteria.

[57]

Concerning the argument that Paquet and Zboch
are “indirectly” violating their non-solicitation obligations, since they have
no direct initial contact with customers, and do not generate business, the
Court finds that, as is the case with Maiore, there is no such breach and that
there is no appearance of right.

[58]

There is no appearance of right to the breach of
confidentiality obligations of these two defendants’ argument.

D.

Serious or irreparable prejudice

[59]

Traffic Tech argues that there
is a potential permanent loss of customers, prospective customers and business
relations for Traffic Tech due to the defendant’s unlawful actions, which could
also cause irreparable harm to Traffic Tech
[27]
.

[60]

At the provisional
injunction stage, speculation and vague assertions are not sufficient
[28]
.

[61]

Traffic Tech cannot pretend
to the exclusivity of its customers. If certain matters have been
inappropriately diverted by Traffix, there will be time to establish the
damages so suffered.

[62]

Traffic Tech has filed under
seal figures quantifying its damages. This quantification and their relative
size point to their “reparable” character. Traffic Tech has boasted about its
size, being an international company with as many as 1000 employees. While this
would not be a justification by defendants for breaching their obligations, it
does put any damages into perspective and militates against their “irreparable”
or even “serious” character.

[63]

The Court is not satisfied
that Traffic Tech will suffer irreparable harm following Paquet and Zboch’s
resignation and joining Traffix.

E.

Balance of Convenience

[64]

Given the lack of irreparable harm, it is
unnecessary to examine the balance of convenience. In light of Traffic Tech’s
size compared to the defendants’ livelihood, the latter would have been
favoured.

CONCLUSION

FOR
THESE REASONS, THE COURT:

[65]

DISMISSES
the application for an order for
provisional injunction
.

[66]

WITH COSTS.
